deals.evidence: American John Berylson leads a takeover of the club, becoming major shareholder and Chairman.
deals.headline: John Berylson leads takeover of Millwall
deals.summary: American John Berylson led a takeover of the club in 2007, becoming major shareholder and chairman. Before the brief's 2015 window but the transaction behind the current ownership; terms not stated.

deals.evidence: During the year 1570 ordinary shares were issued for cash raising £15.7m of funds for the Company.
deals.headline: Owners subscribe £15.7m of new Millwall Holdings shares
deals.investor: Chestnut Hill Ventures LLC and certain directors
deals.summary: Funding needs in 2024/25 were met by CHV and certain directors subscribing 1,570 new £10,000 ordinary shares at par (£15.7m). CHV also provides a £20m facility (£10m drawn at 30 June 2025), interest-free to 30 June 2026 and repayable 1 July 2027; loan notes held by directors and associates total £10.5m with CHV's. Further allotments followed (share capital £139.56m after 30 June 2026).

deals.evidence: Millwall reached an agreement in principle with the council over the deal in May 2024.
deals.headline: Millwall sign 999-year lease on The Den with Lewisham Council
deals.summary: Millwall and Lewisham Council signed a 999-year lease on The Den and surrounding land, giving the club development rights; agreed in principle in May 2024. Terms not stated.

deals.evidence: in January 2025 the club purchased its first team and under 21s training facility at Calmont Road
deals.headline: Millwall buy the freehold of the Calmont Road training ground
deals.summary: In January 2025 the club bought its first-team and under-21 training facility at Calmont Road, ending a sale-and-leaseback in place since 2006; price not stated.

attendance.evidence: Average league attendance for the year was 15,497 compared to an average of 16,544 in 2024

notes: millwallfc.co.uk renders client-side; its content is cited from the club's own CMS API (pages.cms.web.gc.millwallfcservices.co.uk / news.cms.web.gc.millwallfcservices.co.uk), which serves the same text as the public pages (e.g. millwallfc.co.uk/club-information/history, /club-information/whos-who, /news/2025/december/22/...). Companies House accounts cited in their iXBRL (xhtml) form; the PDF versions are scanned images. Financials are the group (Millwall Holdings Limited, 02355508): turnover £23,853k, operating profit £1,242k after a record £21.6m profit on player trading (Esse, Flemming), loss before tax £263k; the club company alone shows turnover £23,855,359 and profit before tax £184,799. No official stadium capacity found on a citable page (club news: record league attendance 19,639 v West Ham, 19 Sep 2026). No stake percentages are stated: CHV is 'majority shareholder'/'principal shareholder'; the PSC register lists only James Berylson (significant influence or control, including over trustees of a trust). Investor_type 'family_office' for CHV is our reading of a Berylson family investment vehicle, not a page's label. SBK is principal partner on back of shirt and shorts for 2026/27. Reached the 2026 Championship play-offs (semi-final v Hull City, who went on to win promotion) and remains in the Championship for 2026/27. No valuation, net debt figure, honours count or social counts found.

owners.evidence: Has significant influence or control over the trustees of a trust
owners.name: James Berylson

ownership_summary: Controlled by the Berylson family through Chestnut Hill Ventures LLC (USA), the majority shareholder of Millwall Holdings Limited, which owns the club company; CHV is ultimately controlled jointly by chairman James Berylson and R A Smith as trustee of a family will trust. John Berylson led the 2007 takeover; James Berylson succeeded him as the registered person with significant control in July 2023. Several directors are minority shareholders who subscribe for new shares alongside CHV.
